topic: What if your strength doubled every day?

script.text: By day twelve, your face is on every news channel. Scientists argue about you on TV. One says you're a hoax. Another says you're the most important person alive.

That afternoon, there's a black car parked outside your house, engine running. A man in a grey suit rings the doorbell. Mum opens the door. He smiles at you over her shoulder. 'We've been watching your friend's videos.'

He sits down at the kitchen table and does the maths out loud. 'Today, two hundred tonnes. In ten more days, a cargo ship. And on day twenty-seven, the Great Pyramid of Giza.' That one's real too. The Great Pyramid weighs about six million tonnes. Fifty kilos, doubled twenty-seven times, is six point seven million.
'We can help you,' he says. 'Doctors. Control training. A safe place to live.' He slides a contract across the table. The table bends under your elbow.
He knows things he shouldn't. Your shoe size. Your school. Which hand cracked.
'And in return?' He smiles again. 'In return, you help us. Ships. Rubble. Things no machine can move.' He pauses. 'And a few things we'd rather not talk about in front of your mother.'
That night, Mo whispers through the phone. 'Bro. They don't want to help you. They want a weapon.'
You told the man you needed time to think. He left a card. But before his car pulled away, you heard him on the phone. 'No. Not yet. But by day twenty, nobody will be able to stop him.'

science.claim: Fifty kilos doubled twenty-seven times is about 6.7 million tonnes, more than the Great Pyramid of Giza (about six million tonnes).
science.working: 50 kg x 2^27 = 6,710,886,400 kg = 6.7 million t. The Great Pyramid's mass is usually estimated at about 6 million tonnes.
science.source: Arithmetic; Encyclopaedia Britannica, Pyramids of Giza

science.claim: On day twelve you can lift about two hundred tonnes.
